The 1880 US Census household of Henry Applegarth in Goodhue County, MN is already cited on the FS person record (source 9ZFC-NJH). It should show John Edward ('Eddie') living with his parents Henry and Nancy Applegarth. As a household census it is also the primary source for identifying older and younger siblings still at home. This is the highest-yield single record for both parents and siblings.

The 1885 Minnesota State Census record (source S8G4-YXS) cites John Edward ('Edward') in the household of H W Applegarth and Nancy J Applegarth. Corroborates the 1880 finding and may show different siblings — those born between 1880 and 1885, or older children who were absent in 1880.

John Edward Applegarth's 1949 California death record (source S8XS-LQC) names Henry Applegarth as father. A death certificate is derivative information about parents (informant unlikely to have personal knowledge of grandparents), but it independently corroborates the census evidence and may supply the mother's name and additional details about Henry.

Search the 1870 US Census for Henry Applegarth in Minnesota (Goodhue County, where John was born in 1878). This record would show the family roughly eight years before John's birth, including any older siblings born before 1870 who are central to sibling identification. Also confirms Henry and Nancy as a couple before John's birth.

Search Minnesota marriage records for the marriage of Henry Applegarth and Nancy J. (surname unknown). A dedicated search for the parents' marriage record is required for a parentage plan: it confirms the couple as a unit, supplies the mother's maiden name (which census records omit), and by its date relative to John's 1878 birth corroborates the parent-child identification. Fallback: search Ancestry for Minnesota marriage indexes.

The 1865 Minnesota State Census (source S2BB-M1M) cites 'William C Applegarth and Nancy J Applegarth' — potentially Henry's father or an older sibling. Reading this record clarifies the extended Applegarth family structure and may reveal older siblings or the grandfather, grounding the parentage chain. The 1851 Canada census (7DQS-XYM) for 'William Applegarth' may also illuminate the prior generation.

The Applegarth Family Website (sources 9K68-ZSY and 9K6C-C8T at sites.rootsmagic.com/Applegarth) is a compiled genealogy. Under BCG Standard 13, treat as a lead, not a conclusion: review it to identify sibling names and cross-check against original records. It may name siblings not yet captured in the FS tree.

**Conclusion (Proved):** John Edward Applegarth (b. 16 December 1878, Pine Island, Goodhue County, Minnesota; d. 5 November 1949, Los Angeles, California; FamilySearch ID KZJT-4PT) was the son of **Henry W. Applegarth** (b. about 1837, Canada) and **Nancy J. Clark Applegarth** (b. about 1842, New York).

### Evidence Summary

**1880 United States Census** (original record; S1). Eddie Applegarth (b. ~1878, MN) is listed as "Son" in the household of Henry Applegarth (head, b. ~1837, Canada) and Nancy Applegarth (wife, b. ~1842, New York), Pine Island, Goodhue County, Minnesota, with siblings William, Alfina, Lewis, and Mary. The 1880 census relationship column — introduced that year — directly states the parent-child bond. The informant is unidentified but classified as indeterminate quality per standard census practice; any household member would have firsthand knowledge of the family's composition. This record provides direct evidence of the parent-child relationship from an original source.

**1885 Minnesota State Census** (original record; S2). Edward Applegarth (b. ~1878, MN) appears as a child of H W Applegarth (head, b. ~1837, Canada) and Nancy J Applegarth (wife, b. ~1842, New York) in the same Pine Island, Goodhue County household, now also including Andrew (b. ~1882). A different enumerator, a different census year, and the same consistent parentage — this is an independent corroborating original record.

**1949 California Death Certificate** (original record; S3). The Los Angeles County death record for John Edward Applegarth explicitly names "Henry Applegarth" as father and gives the mother's maiden surname as "Clark." The informant was the surviving spouse Frances Applegarth, who lacked firsthand knowledge of John's birth — making this secondary information — but the death certificate provides direct evidence by explicitly naming the father. The different informant class makes this a second independent corroboration.

### Corroborating Evidence

The **1870 United States Census** (original; S4) places H W Applegarth (b. ~1837, Canada) and Nancy Applegarth (b. ~1842, New York) as a married couple in Dodge County, Minnesota, with children William (b. ~1862) and Eliza A. (b. ~1870) — eight years before John Edward's birth, confirming the parental couple was established in Minnesota well before 1878.

FAN-cluster evidence from Nebraska marriage records (searched as pli_006 collateral finds) shows "Henry W Applegarth" and "Nancy J Clark" named as parents in the marriages of their children Lewis, William, and Andrew — independent evidence from a third record series that these individuals are recognized as the parents of multiple Applegarth children of this household.

### Source Classification Summary

All four records are **original** sources (census schedules and the county death record itself). The census parentage designations carry **direct** evidence type (relationship column / household position) with **indeterminate** information quality (unknown informant). The death certificate parentage data carries **direct** evidence type with **secondary** information quality (surviving spouse as informant). No derivative sources are relied upon for the concluded fact.

### Exhaustiveness and Overturn Risk

Research was declared reasonably exhaustive (see q_001 exhaustive_declaration). The marriage record for Henry and Nancy was not located on FamilySearch; the marriage predates Minnesota residence and likely lies in Canadian or New York archives. Finding that record would corroborate rather than alter the conclusion. No record type exists that is likely to name a different father. Overturn risk is low.

### Conclusion

Three independent original records from three different record series (federal census, state census, state vital record), supported by corroborating evidence from a fourth original record and FAN-cluster collateral sources, converge without conflict on **Henry W. Applegarth** (b. ~1837, Canada) and **Nancy J. Clark Applegarth** (b. ~1842, New York) as the parents of John Edward Applegarth. All five GPS components are satisfied. **Tier: Proved.**

All five siblings are children of Henry W. Applegarth (born about 1837, Canada) and Nancy J. Clark Applegarth (born about 1842, New York) — the parents established as proved under q_001. Siblinghood with John Edward follows from co-residence in the same household across three census years.

**1885 Minnesota State Census — Pine Island, Goodhue County (second full-family observation).** The household of H. W. Applegarth lists: Alzina (age ~15, born 1870 MN), Lewis (age ~12, born 1873 MN), Mary (age ~10, born 1875 MN), Edward [John Edward] (age ~7, born 1878 MN), and Andrew (age ~3, born 1882 MN).² William's absence is consistent with his age (~23 by 1885, likely having left home). No conflicting evidence was encountered. Minor birth-year discrepancies — Lewis (~1874 in 1880 vs. ~1873 in 1885) and Mary (~1876 in 1880 vs. ~1875 in 1885) — fall within the normal range of census age rounding and do not constitute conflicts requiring resolution.

### Confidence Tier: Proved

Three original census records spanning 1870–1885, all within the same Goodhue County locality, consistently identify the same sibling set in the Applegarth household.
